data.note:
Reflection note: Specimen s_07f98c80cd unblinded as cytochalasin D (PubChem CID 5458428, ChEMBL260287, no curated ChEMBL mechanism; BBBC021 annotation Actin disruptors). My conclusion Eg5 inhibitors was incorrect; protocol NSC vote was 2/4 Eg5 inhibitors vs 1 Actin disruptors, 1 Protein synthesis, reflecting split evidence.

Phenotype was strongly dose-dependent cell rounding/retraction with massive actin heterogeneity (act_std z 25.9 at 0.1 µM → 168.7 at 3 µM, Spearman rho=1.0, e12) and tubulin texture increase (tub_glcm_contrast rho=1.0, e11), plus apparent mitotic-like fraction increase (rho=1.0, e9) and reduced cell area (rho=-1.0, e13) and nuclear solidity drop. Microscopist described bright condensed yellow overlap, punctate tubulin, condensed irregular nuclei, and flagged antimitotic/microtubule destabilizer-like mitotic arrest, but noted inability to distinguish destabilizer vs stabilizer vs Eg5/Aurora on composites alone (e4).

Literature now retrieved clarifies: cytochalasin D caps and severs actin filaments (Mitani et al, PNAS 2025, PMID 40658853) and inhibits actin-cofilin interaction (Shoji et al, BBRC 2012, PMID 22728040), producing patchy cortical actin, contractile rounding, and secondary tubulin condensation in the contracted cell body that elevates tub_mean/glcm contrast and mimics mitotic texture. The frac_mitotic_like signal likely reflects condensed rounded nuclei/segmentation artifact and transient multinucleate proxy (9.86 at 0.1 µM) rather than true sustained monopolar arrest; lack of dose-dependent frac_multinucleate_proxy (rho -0.8, e14) and frac_large_nucleus decline argued against Aurora/Eg5 polyploidy but was insufficiently weighted. Atlas neighbors showed Actin disruptors mean similarity 0.57-0.59 (e5/e8) close to Eg5, with low absolute similarities (~0.60), indicating weak discriminative power.

Learning: for future actin disruptor vs antimitotic disambiguation, prioritize direct actin phenotype (act_std/glcm) plus orthogonal monopolar

reflection.text:
We called Eg5 inhibitors p=0.58, truth was Actin disruptors (cytochalasin D, PubChem CID 5458428). We and the protocol were both wrong. Review verdict approve was correct that this was a weak call - 2/4 NSC vote, neighbors 5/10 Eg5 - but we still mis-ranked it.

What the evidence got right:
- The low-mid dose well w_b617e84d8d (0.3 uM, rep1) was correctly nearest Actin disruptors similarity 0.63 (e5, protocol per-well tally). That well already showed the true signal: act_std z=+66.9, act_glcm_contrast z=+50.3, tub_glcm_contrast z=+38.5 (e2). At 0.1 uM we also saw nuc_solidity z=-78.3 with act_glcm_contrast +30.2 / act_std +25.9 (e7) - early actin texture change before full collapse.
- The atlas k-neighbours never lost Actin: 3/10 Actin at 2 wells (e5) and 3/10 Actin at 4 wells (e8). Our hypothesis board kept Actin disruptors at 0.12 (e16) but we underweighted it.
- After unblinding, that actin signal matches the known mechanism: cytochalasin D caps and severs actin filaments PMID 40658853 and acts as inhibitor of actin-cofilin interaction PMID 22728040. The extreme dose-dependent act_std rho=+1.00 p=0 (e12) to z=+139.0 at 1 uM (e6) and z=+168.7 at 3 uM (e3) was the direct readout of that, not secondary.

What misled us and why:
- frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0 (e9) from 0.098 to 0.37, plus cell_area rho=-1.00 p=0 (e13) and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 (e11) to z=+140.0 at 3 uM (e3) / +138.7 at 1 uM (e6). We read this triad - dose-dependent "mitotic" fraction + rounding + tubulin condensation - as antimitotic Eg5/microtubule, and e16 supporting evidence cited e9/e11/e4 for Eg5 0.58. In retrospect actin depolymerization drives cell contraction/rounding and cytoplasmic densification, which the image proxy scores as mitotic-like and produces high tubulin texture via cell collapse, not monopolar spindles. No paper in this run supported "actin collapse looks mitotic" (search e21 returned 0 hits), so we had no literature anchor to discount e9.
- Atlas flip at high dose. The two high-dose wells w_e741eff746 1 uM similarity 0.599 and w_2992baa437 3 uM similarity 0.575 both voted Eg5 (protocol per-well), overtaking the one correct Actin vote. That gave NSC 2/4 Eg5 vs 1/4 Actin vs 1/4 Protein synthesis (e8, protocol tally summed similarity 1.174 vs 0.63). k-neighbours 5/10 Eg5 at 4 wells reinforced it. We took that majority as tie-breaker despite low similarities <0.63 and weak 2/4 split noted in review.
- describe_phenotype e4: "density lower vs DMSO; 10 observations; candidates: Microtubule destabilizers". The microscopist framed it as antimitotic, not actin collapse, and our update_hypotheses e16 used e4 as support for Eg5 and Microtubule destabilizers 0.22. Visual review could not split Eg5 vs microtubule destabilizers per review critique, and it pushed us away from Actin.
- We mis-used negative controls. frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.80 (e14) and frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 (e15) plus nuc_solidity rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10) correctly argued against Aurora/polyploidy, but we treated "not Aurora" as "therefore Eg5" rather than as nondiscriminative between Eg5 and actin-induced rounding.

Acquisition choices:
- We sampled 4 wells covering doses 3-6 (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 uM) per e1 inventory of 8 doses 0.003-10 uM, one replicate each, budget 0 left. That biased to the transition-to-saturated range where contraction dominates. The 0.1 uM well went to Protein synthesis (0.599) - transitional. We never sampled the lowest doses 1-2 or highest 7-8 where actin dose-onset vs saturated Eg5 mimic might have diverged, and we had no rep2 to test stability of the 0.63 Actin call.
- We ran many dose_response tests (e9-e15) but all were morphological proxies from the same 4 wells, so they were not independent validation. A mechanistic assay as we proposed - alpha-tubulin + pericentrin/DAPI for monopolar vs bipolar spindles, plus Eg5 ATPase assay - was needed to distinguish, not another texture correlation.

Lesson: We gave too much weight to a generic mitotic-like/area/tubulin-texture triad that actin disruptors phenocopy at high dose, and too little to the earliest, most specific signal - the 0.3 uM Actin vote with act_std +66.9 already present and rising monotonically. With a 2/4 vote we should have stayed near 0.3-0.4 for Eg5 or flagged as unresolved Actin/Eg5 ambiguity, not 0.58 Eg5 vs 0.12 Actin.
what_was_right: Low-mid dose w_b617e84d8d 0.3 uM correctly voted Actin disruptors similarity 0.63 (e5) with act_std z=+66.9 and act_glcm_contrast +50.3 (e2) - direct actin capping/severing signal per PMID 40658853 and actin-cofilin inhibition PMID 22728040
Actin texture was dose-dependent act_std rho=+1.00 and act_glcm_contrast high at 1 uM (+104.4) and 3 uM (+119.3) z-scores (e3,e6,e12) - consistent with truth, not Eg5-specific
Atlas k-neighbours retained 3/10 Actin at both 2-well and 4-well comparisons (e5,e8) - we kept hypothesis but underweighted
what_was_wrong: High-dose wells 1 uM and 3 uM flipped to Eg5 inhibitors similarity 0.599/0.575 (protocol per-well) giving weak 2/4 NSC majority (e8) that we treated as decisive for Eg5 0.58 (e16,e17)

Interpreted frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 (e9), cell_area rho=-1.00 (e13), tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 to z=+140 (e11,e3) as mitotic arrest/Eg5, when actin-induced rounding/contraction phenocopies it - search for actin rounding mitotic artifact returned 0 hits (e21)
Microscopist e4 microtubule destabilizer call biased toward antimitotic interpretation, used as support for Eg5 (e16)

Used lack of multinucleation/large nucleus (e14 rho=-0.80, e15 rho=-0.80) to exclude Aurora but not to question Eg5, and ignored nuc_solidity rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10) inconsistent with true mitotic condensation
Sampling only doses 3-6 (0.1-3 uM) with 1 replicate each to budget 0 (e1, review) missed low-dose onset and high-dose saturation that might have clarified actin vs Eg5 mimicry

citations.claim: cytochalasin D caps/severs actin filaments - matches act_std/act_glcm_contrast phenotype we downweighted
cytochalasin D inhibits actin-cofilin interaction - supports actin disruptor mechanism

We took that majority as tie-breaker despite low similarities <0.63 and weak 2/4 split noted in review.
- describe_phenotype e4: "density lower vs DMSO; 10 observations; candidates: Microtubule destabilizers". The microscopist framed it as antimitotic, not actin collapse, and our update_hypotheses e16 used e4 as support for Eg5 and Microtubule destabilizers 0.22. Visual review could not split Eg5 vs microtubule destabilizers per review critique, and it pushed us away from Actin.
- We mis-used negative controls. frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.80 (e14) and frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 (e15) plus nuc_solidity rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10) correctly argued against Aurora/polyploidy, but we treated "not Aurora" as "therefore Eg5" rather than as nondiscriminative between Eg5 and actin-induced rounding.

Acquisition choices:
- We sampled 4 wells covering doses 3-6 (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 uM) per e1 inventory of 8 doses 0.003-10 uM, one replicate each, budget 0 left. That biased to the transition-to-saturated range where contraction dominates. The 0.1 uM well went to Protein synthesis (0.599) - transitional. We never sampled the lowest doses 1-2 or highest 7-8 where actin dose-onset vs saturated Eg5 mimic might have diverged, and we had no rep2 to test stability of the 0.63 Actin call.
- We ran many dose_response tests (e9-e15) but all were morphological proxies from the same 4 wells, so they were not independent validation. A mechanistic assay as we proposed - alpha-tubulin + pericentrin/DAPI for monopolar vs bipolar spindles, plus Eg5 ATPase assay - was needed to distinguish, not another texture correlation.

Lesson: We gave too much weight to a generic mitotic-like/area/tubulin-texture triad that actin disruptors phenocopy at high dose, and too little to the earliest, most specific signal - the 0.3 uM Actin vote with act_std +66.9 already present and rising monotonically. With a 2/4 vote we should have stayed near 0.3-0.4 for Eg5 or flagged as unresolved Actin/Eg5 ambiguity, not 0.58 Eg5 vs 0.12 Actin.

What was right:
- Low-mid dose w_b617e84d8d 0.3 uM correctly voted Actin disruptors similarity 0.63 (e5) with act_std z=+66.9 and act_glcm_contrast +50.3 (e2) - direct actin capping/severing signal per PMID 40658853 and actin-cofilin inhibition PMID 22728040
- Actin texture was dose-dependent act_std rho=+1.00 and act_glcm_contrast high at 1 uM (+104.4) and 3 uM (+119.3) z-scores (e3,e6,e12) - consistent with truth, not Eg5-specific
- Atlas k-neighbours retained 3/10 Actin at both 2-well and 4-well comparisons (e5,e8) - we kept hypothesis but underweighted

What was wrong or missed:
- High-dose wells 1 uM and 3 uM flipped to Eg5 inhibitors similarity 0.599/0.575 (protocol per-well) giving weak 2/4 NSC majority (e8) that we treated as decisive for Eg5 0.58 (e16,e17)
- Interpreted frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 (e9), cell_area rho=-1.00 (e13), tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 to z=+140 (e11,e3) as mitotic arrest/Eg5, when actin-induced rounding/contraction phenocopies it - search for actin rounding mitotic artifact returned 0 hits (e21)
- Microscopist e4 microtubule destabilizer call biased toward antimitotic interpretation, used as support for Eg5 (e16)
- Used lack of multinucleation/large nucleus (e14 rho=-0.80, e15 rho=-0.80) to exclude Aurora but not to question Eg5, and ignored nuc_solidity rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10) inconsistent with true mitotic condensation
- Sampling only doses 3-6 (0.1-3 uM) with 1 replicate each to budget 0 (e1, review) missed low-dose onset and high-dose saturation that might have clarified actin vs Eg5 mimicry

Proposed next experiment: Immunofluorescence for monopolar vs bipolar spindles (alpha-tubulin + pericentrin/DAPI) at 0.1-3 uM vs reference Eg5 inhibitor and cytochalasin D controls, plus phalloidin actin integrity and in vitro Eg5 ATPase assay - would directly test Eg5 vs actin/microtubule destabilizer as we proposed.
